Graphical summaries

Histograms
If we want to make the histogram from the morley data that we saw in lecture, then we can use the ggplot and geom_boxplot functions from the tidyverse suite of packages:








The ggplot2 package uses a grammar for graphics. The first function ggplot() takes two arguments: the data to be plotted (morley) and the aesthetics for the plot. In this case, we are choosing to put Speed on the x-axis. Switching to the y-axis is easy:








The second function, geom_histogram tells R which plot to make; in this case, it is a histogram. We then give few additional arguments which allow us to customize how the histogram looks.








Recall that changing the width of the histogram bins can have a large effect on how we interpret the histogram. The easiest way to do this using geom_histogram is by using the bins= argument. For example, we can enter:

Converting it into a tibble
Usually we think of our data being organized into columns representing variables and rows representing individual observations. The UCBAdmisions data is not quite in this format, but we can use the tibble data structure from the tidyverse suite of packages to make it into something more useful.








We can see there are four columns: Admit, Gender, Dept and n, where n is the count of the number of applications in each group defined by a combination of the three other variables.

title: Topic 1: Getting Started
text:
What is RStudio?
RStudio is the most popular integrated development environment (IDE) for the R statistical software. Many find the user interface easier to work with as it allows for straightforward editing of files, interaction with the R console and graphical interfaces for working with directory file structures, plots and many other tools.

title: Topic 1: Getting Started
text:
How do I use these?
It is very important to follow these steps

First, install the R Statistical package.

You can dowload R from one of the Canadian repositories, like the repository at the University of Waterloo. Make sure you download the correct software for your computing platform.



Second, install RStudio.

Only after R is installed, then you can download the installation of R Studio for your computing platform.. Make sure you click the button to download RStudio.

title: Topic 1: Getting Started
text:
Other options
However, if you just to fool around with R, you have some other choices.

Using Posit Cloud
Posit (the company who created RStudio) allows you to run RStudio and R directly from their cloud servers for free (with certain computing and collaboration alternatives). You will need to set up an account, but you can work in RStudio without having to install anything on your home machine.


But if this is all too overwhelming…
I have also decided to set up some webpages where you can interact with R all in your own browser, writing and testing code without even having an account on Posit Cloud! But once you feel comfortable with R from my tutorial pages, you may want to unleash the full power of R and RStudio by installing them yourself.
